## 2026-09-10 — Verdict, campaign C T2 matched-count diversity (float32): replacing half of 435 DrivAerML cars with estate cars cuts the fastback error 84% (ISLA) and 81% (GeoTransolver) but costs 32% and 19% in-family; a trade, not a free lever {#sec-nb-campc-t2-verdict}

**Setting.** T2 of campaign C (`studies/campaign_c_transfer/PREREG.md`)
holds the training-set size at 435 cases and swaps composition: 218
DrivAerML plus 217 SHIFT-SUV estate cars (drawn deterministically, seed
2026) against the all-DrivAerML reference runs, for ISLA and the unit-drive
GeoTransolver, two seeds each, frozen protocol. Readouts in float32:
zero-shot surface-pressure relative L2 on the 99 SHIFT-SUV fastback
validation cases (a third family, seen by neither arm) and the in-family
DrivAerML validation error (48 cars). The references are the existing
single-family checkpoints (`iw_mt2_lr1e3_seed{42,43}`,
`uw_gt_unit_lr1e3_seed{42,43}`) evaluated under the snapshot that wrote them
(@sec-nb-snapshot-hazard). Bar: diversity HELPS if the fastback error falls
by ≥ 30% at ≤ 10% in-family cost; otherwise the trade is reported.

**Readout (seed means; artifact
`studies/campaign_c_transfer/campaign_c_t2_2026-09-10.json`).**

| arm | fastback pressure | fastback wall shear | fastback drag rel. MAE | DrivAerML pressure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA, 435 DrivAerML (reference) | 0.788 (0.782, 0.794) | 1.327 | 1.61 | 0.0557 |
| ISLA, 218 DrivAerML + 217 estate | 0.128 (0.129, 0.126) | 0.157 | 0.16 | 0.0737 |
| GeoTransolver unit drive, 435 DrivAerML (reference) | 0.612 (0.609, 0.615) | 1.397 | 1.56 | 0.0504 |
| GeoTransolver unit drive, 218 DrivAerML + 217 estate | 0.115 (0.109, 0.121) | 0.141 | 0.13 | 0.0598 |

: Drag: the recipe's integrated drag coefficient, mean absolute error over the reference mean; the zero-shot references are off by more than the coefficient itself. {#tbl-campc-t2}

**Verdict: diversity helps on the target at an in-family cost above the
bar, for both architectures; the preregistered "helps" clause is not met
and the trade is reported.** The fastback error drops 84% (ISLA, 0.788 →
0.128) and 81% (GeoTransolver, 0.612 → 0.115), six to seven times the 30%
bar, and the drag error goes from unusable (> 100%) to 13–16%. The price
is paid in the family that lost half its training cars: DrivAerML error
rises 32% for ISLA (0.0557 → 0.0737) and 19% for GeoTransolver (0.0504 →
0.0598), against the 10% bar. Two readings. First, the estate cars carry
the fastback family's conventions (same simulation, ground and wheel
treatment, different body), so 217 of them substitute for the 794 the
program had used before: the mixed 435-case models reach 0.128 and 0.115
on the fastback cases against 0.11–0.13 for the historical DrivAerML +
794-estate training, so the estate coverage saturates fast. Second, the
in-family cost is not symmetric between architectures: GeoTransolver
gives up 19% to gain the second family, ISLA 32%, consistent with the
few-shot reading (@sec-nb-campc-t3-verdict) that ISLA's DrivAerML fit is
more family-specific; but note that the per-family data halved for both,
so part of the cost is the 218-car rung of each architecture's own
data ladder, not the mixing.

**What changes.** For the program's transfer question the practical
statement is: with a fixed label budget, spending half of it on the target
convention's sibling family buys the target family almost entirely and
costs a fifth to a third of the source family's accuracy; the mixed-family
model is the deployable one if both families matter, the single-family
model if only the source does. The remaining T1 arms (complete
conditioning, four lanes still training) ask whether a per-case condition
input recovers part of that in-family cost by letting the model tell the
two conventions apart.

## 2026-09-10 — Program redirect (Peter): principled generalization over in-distribution accuracy; the measure-weights-off configuration is an ablation, never a reference; earlier wording superseded {#sec-nb-redirect}

Peter's ruling, binding for every session of the program: the goal is an
accurate model reached by physically principled means, because those
principles are what generalize to novel problems; accuracy can be bought
later with size, generalization cannot. Concretely, ISLA with its measure
weights off reads the mesher's sampling density in place of the surface
measure, a discretization-dependent signal that would give a different
answer on a uniformly generated point cloud or another mesher, so it stays
an ablation ("what does the measure semantics cost in-distribution, and
what does it buy under a discretization change?") and is never ISLA's
reference or flagship configuration. Every proposed architecture change
must state its mechanism, be physically principled, and pass
discretization-invariance tests (biased resampling, uniform or
area-proportional resampling, a different mesher) before adoption.

Consequences in this companion. The phrases "the program's best fair
configuration" and "recommended for canonical benchmarks" applied to the
weights-off arm in @sec-nb-campe-bf16 and @sec-nb-campe-verdict are
superseded: those entries stand as dated records, and the weights-off row
in their tables is read as the ablation it always was, whose 19x collapse
under the density skew is the discretization dependence made visible.
Campaign A's weights-off arm (@sec-nb-campa-n35) and its pending 210-case
rung are ablations measuring the in-distribution cost of the measure
semantics across draws, not candidates. Chapter 7 is reworded in the same
pass. Audit of this program's own proposals against the ruling: the D1
support set and passive readout are measure-consistent by construction
(the support carries positions, normals and signed distance; the readout
is a measure-normalized kernel; the support's total mass is a learned
fraction of the source measure, not a count) and were tested for
measure-scale and source-refinement invariance before launch; campaign D's
carriers (width; GeoTransolver-volume's radius-based local features) are
capacity questions, and the local-features arm is itself a density-dependent
input whose removal is what the arm measures; the campaign E result is the
ruling's own evidence, since the only density-robust configuration is the
one with the measure-consistent gauge; nothing in this program reads the
query or sample density as a signal. The welcome directions named
(signed distance, signed heat or geodesic distance, curvature, invariances,
measure-consistent operators) are the ones the D1 support set already uses
and the ones the boundary-response and composition gates were built for.

**T2 in-family cost decomposed (addendum to @sec-nb-campc-t2-verdict).**
Four lanes trained on the campaign's own 218 DrivAerML cars alone at the
campaign protocol (500 epochs, lr 1e-3, unit drive for GeoTransolver; two
seeds each; the scaling ladder's existing 218-car checkpoints were not
usable, being lr 3e-3, physical drive and 51 epochs) split the in-family
cost of the mixed 435-case models into a data-rung factor (218 DrivAerML
alone ÷ 435 DrivAerML alone) and a mixing factor (218 + 217 estate ÷ 218
alone), float32, DrivAerML validation pressure:

| architecture | 435 alone | 218 alone | 218 + 217 estate | rung factor | mixing factor | product (= in-family cost) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA | 0.0557 | 0.0683 | 0.0737 | 1.226 | 1.078 | 1.322 |
| GeoTransolver, unit drive | 0.0504 | 0.0573 | 0.0598 | 1.137 | 1.043 | 1.186 |

: The 218-car single-family models score 0.848 (ISLA) and 0.670 (GeoTransolver) zero-shot on the fastback cases, worse than the 435-car ones (0.788, 0.612). Artifact `studies/campaign_c_transfer/campaign_c_t2_2026-09-10.json` (arms `dr218_isla`, `dr218_gt`). {#tbl-campc-t2-decomp}

Most of the cost is the halved source data, not the foreign family: mixing
217 estate cars into 218 DrivAerML cars costs 8% (ISLA) and 4%
(GeoTransolver) in-family, the halving 23% and 14%. So the T2 sentence
becomes: at a fixed label budget, spending half on the target's sibling
family buys the target family almost entirely and costs the source family
about what any halving of its data costs, plus 4–8% for the mixing. ISLA
pays more on both factors (its 218-car rung is steeper and its mixing cost
double GeoTransolver's), the same direction as every other reading of this
campaign. The one-seed conditioning preview (T1, verdict pending)
shows the mixing cost growing with the foreign share: 435 DrivAerML + 794
estate costs ISLA 18% in-family with no halving at all.

## 2026-09-10 — Instrument note: the density-bias probe hands the model an importance-corrected area measure, so its degradation factors are model dependence, not estimator bias {#sec-nb-probe-convention}

Asked by the main session as the probe's author: are the measure weights
under the 10:1 biased draw the raw areas of the sampled cells (a biased
quadrature, which would degrade even a perfectly measure-consistent model)
or importance-corrected? Verified in the code path the surface model sees.
The model receives `interior.point_data._target_quadrature_measure`,
materialized at the mesh-to-domain boundary as `cell_measures(mesh) =
cell_areas × cell_data._measure_weights` (`physicsnemo/mesh/calculus/measure.py`,
called from `datapipes/transforms/mesh/transforms.py`). The weights field is
a multiplicative inclusion ratio composed by every sampling stage: the
reader's uniform 40,000-cell draw contributes N/40,000, a uniform second
stage contributes n_before/n_cells, and the biased second stage
(`PoissonBiasedSubsampleMesh`) contributes exactly 1/π_i per kept cell,
π_i = min(1, c·w_i) with w = 10 on the front half of the car. The saved
artifacts confirm it: under the uniform draw every cell carries the ratio
1,703 (= 17.03M / 10,000); under the biased draw the dense half carries 937
and the sparse half 9,366 (1,703 × 11/20 and × 11/2, the two-region Poisson
design), with totals preserved within Poisson noise. So an exactly
measure-consistent model sees an unbiased Horvitz–Thompson quadrature of
each region; the constant-gauge ISLA's 12x and the weights-off ISLA's 19x
(@sec-nb-campe-verdict) are model dependence on the sampling, the
similarity gauge's 1.21x is the residual of estimator variance plus model.
Two clauses now attach to every density-robustness statement in this
companion: "biased" means biased inclusion with exact importance
correction, and the base measure is the true triangle area, so the probe
is area-consistent and reusable as is for the consistency benchmark (an
area-proportional draw would compose π_i ∝ area_i through the same call).
Also measured for the cross-family study (float32, zero-shot fastback,
under `code`): the similarity-gauge ISLA 0.945 (1.038 / 0.851), the
2,560-anchor query-independent variant 0.850 (0.800 / 0.900), weights off
0.806 (0.802 / 0.811), against the reference 0.788; none of the existing
variants transfers better than the reference, and the gauge's two seeds
differ by 0.19 on this readout (artifacts
`$T/transfer/fastback_zeroshot_fp32/<run>/fastback/`, launcher
`studies/campaign_c_transfer/fastback_zeroshot_variants_aga.sbatch`).

**Mechanism of the constant-gauge collapse, checked against the frozen code
(addendum to @sec-nb-probe-convention).** The main session's derivation
names the unweighted centroid as the one sampling-dependent quantity in the
reference forward pass; verified in the snapshot that trained the reference
(`code/physicsnemo/experimental/nn/mt2/model.py`): the constant-gauge branch
centers by the plain mean of the sampled points (line 513) while the
similarity gauge centers by the measure-weighted mean and scales by the
weighted RMS radius (507–511); slice attention is a softmax over points of
logits plus log measure weights (94, 124, 524), a Horvitz–Thompson
weighting that is unbiased under spatially varying inclusion; the point-to-
slice readback is a softmax over slices with no measure (127, 184); local
features and virtual tokens are off in the reference. The centroid enters
through the per-point seed features (r̂·d̂, r̂·n̂, |r|, lines 533–535) and the
anchor directions; the relational terms r − z are translation-invariant.
Two points added to the main session's preregistered test (weighted
centering at evaluation should recover most of the 12x; falsifier ≥ 6x):
the weighted attention's effective sample size in the sparse half drops
about tenfold under the bias, so a variance residual of the gauge arm's
size (1.21x) remains by construction; and with per-cell area weights the
weighted centroid differs from the plain mean even on the uniform draw, so
the clean comparison is uniform and biased both evaluated with weighted
centering, with the uniform-plain number beside them as the cost of the
frame change. The weights-off arm's 19x adds the loss of the HT weighting
in the attention (log weights zero, line 521) and should not be recovered by
weighted centering alone, a second prediction with a sign.

**Evaluation snapshot (addendum to @sec-nb-snapshot-resolved).** The main
session designated `$T/code_eval` (its scaling branch at 0e41b9ee1: the
raising loader, a legacy class-name search so `MeshTransformer2.*.mdlus`
loads with a warning, the fast kernel as opt-in) as the program-wide
evaluation snapshot after an identity check against `code` (ISLA 1.3 × 10⁻⁶
mean relative difference per case, GeoTransolver and Transolver bitwise).
Every evaluation launcher of this program now sets its PYTHONPATH to
`code_eval` (D1, campaign D, campaigns A, B, C, E, the variant zero-shot
launcher); `code_support` is used for training only; the CLAIMS rule "an
evaluation log containing 'skipping load' voids the run" applies, and an
audit of every evaluation log of this program is running. The hidden-344
evaluation that a watcher had submitted seconds before the edit was
cancelled and resubmitted under the new snapshot (job 700501).

Arm two: GeoTransolver-volume without its six-radius local features (unit

snapshot (`code_eval`) with no skipped loads.

## 2026-09-10 — Diagnostic: ISLA's remaining eddy-viscosity deficit is a far-field effect, not a near-wall one; near the wall ISLA and GeoTransolver-volume are equal on ν_t and ISLA leads on pressure and velocity {#sec-nb-bands}

**Instrument.** Wall-distance band decomposition of the saved float32
interior predictions (`studies/computational_support/band_decomposition.py`;
artifact `band_decomposition_2026-09-10.json`): for every one of the 48
validation cars and each arm, relative L2 over the points in three
signed-distance bands, SDF < 0.01 L (77% of the 10,000 sampled points, the
boundary layer and near wake), 0.01–0.05 L (11.5%), ≥ 0.05 L (10%, the
outer wake and far field), with L the case's reference length, and the
share of each field's squared error carried by each band; two-seed means.
The pooled "all" values here are per-case raw-field relative L2 averaged
over cars and differ by a constant factor from the recipe's standardized
metric (ν_t 0.092 here against 0.1033 there for hidden 344); the ratios
between arms agree (1.18x both ways).

| field, band (share of points) | ISLA h256 | ISLA h344 | GeoTransolver-volume (unit) | GT, no local features |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ν_t, SDF < 0.01 L (77%) | 0.084 | 0.081 | 0.080 | 0.083 |
| ν_t, 0.01–0.05 L (11%) | 0.066 | 0.062 | 0.077 | 0.077 |
| ν_t, ≥ 0.05 L (10%) | 0.101 | 0.093 | 0.068 | 0.071 |
| ν_t, share of squared error in the far band | 46% | 46% | 36% | 36% |
| pressure, SDF < 0.01 L | 0.054 | 0.049 | 0.051 | 0.055 |
| pressure, 0.01–0.05 L | 0.051 | 0.047 | 0.037 | 0.042 |
| pressure, ≥ 0.05 L | 0.094 | 0.082 | 0.067 | 0.077 |
| velocity, SDF < 0.01 L | 0.094 | 0.086 | 0.128 | 0.133 |
| velocity, 0.01–0.05 L | 0.036 | 0.033 | 0.041 | 0.041 |
| velocity, ≥ 0.05 L | 0.042 | 0.040 | 0.033 | 0.035 |

: Pressure and velocity squared errors are 90–94% near-wall for every arm, so their totals are set by the first band; eddy viscosity splits about half and half between the near-wall and far bands for ISLA, 53/36 for GeoTransolver. {#tbl-bands}

**Reading.** The near-wall closure hypothesis is refuted: in the band
where the closure's wall-distance scaling lives, ISLA at matched
parameters and GeoTransolver-volume are equal on eddy viscosity (0.081
against 0.080), and ISLA leads in the intermediate band by 20%. **The whole
18% deficit comes from the far field**: at SDF ≥ 0.05 L ISLA's ν_t error is
0.093 against 0.068, and that band carries 46% of ISLA's squared error
against 36% of GeoTransolver's. Width helped there least (0.101 → 0.093,
against 0.084 → 0.081 near the wall). The same far-field pattern appears
on pressure (0.082 against 0.067) and velocity (0.040 against 0.033), where
it is invisible in the totals because those fields' errors are 90–94%
near-wall. So the picture at matched parameters is: ISLA wins wherever the
surface is close, GeoTransolver wins where it is far. The mechanism this
points at is geometric, not a closure input: far from the body every
surface anchor is at nearly the same distance and direction, so ISLA's
relational invariants to the anchors lose resolution exactly where
GeoTransolver's per-point network on raw position keeps it; the wake is a
far-field structure organized by the drive direction, not by the surface.
The principled candidate under the 2026-09-10 ruling is therefore not a
new closure input but far-field anchors organized by the flow: ISLA already
has an option for latent volume tokens at downstream offsets along the
drive (`latent_volume_tokens`, offsets 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 body lengths), which
is a physically meaningful, discretization-invariant construction (the
wake axis), and its test has a sharp readout: the far-band ν_t error.
Proposed bars for whoever preregisters it, in this table's units at hidden
344: supported if far-band ν_t ≤ 0.074 (within 10% of GeoTransolver's
0.068) with the near-wall band unchanged within 3%; falsified if ≥ 0.085
(no better than the two seeds' 0.087–0.099 range). Not launched by this
track.

## 2026-09-10 — Launched: far-field context tokens for ISLA's interior queries (wake tokens and latent volume tokens at hidden 344), preregistered against the far-band eddy-viscosity error {#sec-nb-wake-launch}

Follow-up to @sec-nb-bands, which located ISLA's remaining interior
eddy-viscosity deficit in the outer wake. Preregistration
`studies/computational_support/PREREG_WAKE.md`, written before any lane.
Two arms, each two seeds, on top of the hidden-344 query-token + SDF
configuration of campaign D (frozen V0 protocol, exact activation
recompute): **wake tokens**, three interacting tokens on the drive axis
through the centering point at 1, 2 and 4 times the measure-weighted RMS
extent of the surface along the drive, and **latent volume tokens**, the
existing off-surface construction (three offsets along each slice anchor's
normal plus the centroid) newly allowed with query tokens. Both are built
covariantly from the surface and the drive alone, are invariant to how the
surface was sampled, carry a routing weight that is a learned fraction of
the total surface measure, and are off by default. Repository commit
e5ff39bea (model and tests: SE(3) covariance, correct output count,
measure-scale and Horvitz–Thompson refinement invariance, liveness,
gradients, constructor contracts, weighted-extent invariance under a 10:1
biased resample); one bookkeeping change rides along, the surface-only
measure statistics and local invariants now use the true surface count
rather than the count after appended context tokens, which is identical
whenever no context tokens are present.

Mechanism stated before the run: far from the body every surface anchor is
at nearly the same distance and direction, so a query's relational
invariants lose the resolution that a per-point network on raw position
keeps; wake tokens add anchors whose relative geometry varies along the
wake (the flow-organized construction), latent volume tokens add
off-surface anchors around the body (the control that says whether any
off-surface context or the wake alignment carries the effect). Bars in the
band-decomposition units: far-band ν_t ≤ 0.074 with the near-wall band
unchanged within 3% → supported; ≥ 0.085 → falsified; between reported as
the fraction of the 0.093 → 0.068 gap closed. Lanes v0wk-0..3
(`v0_isla_qtsdf_h344_{wake,lvt}_seed{42,43}`), code snapshot
`$T/code_wake` (= `code_support` plus the commit), launcher
`v0/v0_wake_aga.sbatch`, evaluation `v0/v0_wake_eval_aga.sbatch` in float32
under `code_wake` (the program's evaluation snapshot does not carry the
option yet; both snapshots evaluate the campaign D reference identically,
so the comparison is same-snapshot in the sense of the CLAIMS rule).

**Where the wake tokens sit (addendum to @sec-nb-wake-launch).** Computed
from the saved surfaces of three validation cars
(`transfer/wake_positions.py`; drive +x; measure = triangle area × inclusion
ratio): the measure-weighted RMS extent of the vehicle along the drive is
ℓ = 0.29 body lengths (bodies 0.84–0.92 L_ref long, L_ref = 5 m); the
weighted centre lies 0.51–0.57 body lengths from the nose and the rear
1.5–1.7 ℓ behind the centre. The three tokens therefore land at 0.29, 0.58
and 1.16 body lengths behind the centre: the first inside the body over
the rear deck (0.14–0.20 L ahead of the rear), the second just behind the
rear (+0.09 to +0.15 L, the near wake), the third 0.67–0.73 body lengths
behind the rear (about 3.5 m, the outer wake). A unit note for
@sec-nb-bands: its "L" is L_ref (the pipeline's coordinates are already
divided by L_ref), so the far band SDF ≥ 0.05 L begins 25 cm from the
surface and the car is 0.92 L long; the two downstream tokens sit in that
band and the first anchors the rear body. Both facts go into the verdict
table beside the four lanes' band decompositions.

## 2026-09-10 — Verdict, D1 computational support with passive readout (float32): FALSIFIED — SUPPORT-12 pressure 0.078 against a bar of 0.060 (1.43x the interacting reference), eddy viscosity 2.4x; depth and support each buy about 12% and neither closes the gap {#sec-nb-d1-verdict}

**Readout** (48 DrivAerML validation cars, float32, two-seed means; arms
and bars from `studies/computational_support/PREREG.md`, bars evaluated at
the float32 reference per @sec-nb-fp32-interior; artifact
`studies/computational_support/d1_verdict_2026-09-10.json`; no skipped
loads in any evaluation log; the D1 arms' 5,000 scored points verified to be
exactly the second half of the reference's 10,000-point sample on the
checked cars, the preregistered check 2 of @sec-nb-evalpoints).

| arm | pressure (seeds) | velocity | eddy viscosity | step [s], memory (unpinned) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (i) reference, query tokens + SDF, 10k interacting queries | 0.0547 | 0.0796 | 0.1116 | 0.28 pinned, 6.1 GB |
| (ii) SUPPORT-12 | 0.0781 (0.0774, 0.0788) | 0.1068 | 0.2689 | 0.71–0.75, 10.8 GB |
| (iii) SUPPORT-4 | 0.0896 (0.0877, 0.0914) | 0.1187 | 0.2485 | 0.67–0.87, 7.1 GB |
| (iv) PASSIVE-12 | 0.0890 (0.0880, 0.0899) | 0.1201 | 0.2305 | 0.62–0.63, 5.9 GB |
| bars at the float32 reference | supported ≤ 0.0563 · falsified ≥ 0.0602 | ≤ 0.0820 | ≤ 0.1149 | |

: SUPPORT-12 ÷ reference: 1.43 / 1.34 / 2.41. Depth (SUPPORT-4 ÷ SUPPORT-12): 1.15 / 1.11 / 0.92. Interaction on a support (PASSIVE-12 ÷ SUPPORT-12): 1.14 / 1.13 / 0.86. bf16 inflation of the arms 2–4% on pressure and velocity. {#tbl-d1-verdict}

**Verdict: falsified**, by the preregistered pressure clause with a wide
margin and on every field. The decomposition says each ingredient of the
passive route is worth about 12–15% on pressure and velocity (twelve read
blocks against four; an interacting 5,000-point support against none) and
nothing on eddy viscosity, which is worse with the support than without;
together they leave the passive route 43% behind the interacting queries
on pressure and 52% behind GeoTransolver-volume. The sentinel-query study
(readout 2) was not run: the accuracy half is falsified, query independence
of the passive path is exact by construction and by test, and its result
could not have moved the verdict. Cost, for the record: the passive route
is also slower (0.71–0.75 s per step unpinned against 0.28 s pinned for the
reference, about 1.9x like for like) and heavier (10.8 GB against 6.1 GB).

**Reading.** The audit's first direction rested on the idea that the
interacting queries supply a rich, geometry-aware computational state that a
problem-derived support could supply instead. The support supplies the
geometry (5,000 interior points with signed distance and gradient are as
geometry-aware as the queries were) and the readout sees the final slice
states, the anchors and a kernel over every token, yet eddy viscosity is 2.4x
worse. What the interacting queries provide is computation at the requested
points, refined through every encoder layer by attention with the other
tokens, which a read block over a finished state does not reproduce. That is
the alternative reading the audit itself flagged, and it is the one the data
support. Consequences: the deployment repair for the query-set dependence
goes through query-count augmentation (main program, QCOUNT), not
architecture; the passive route at matched depth and inputs is closed for
ISLA in this program; the D1 code (support tokens, passive read blocks,
`SplitInteriorSupport`) stays in the repository as the runnable record of a
refuted configuration. Chapter @sec-computational-support is written from
this entry.

## 2026-09-10 — Verdict, campaign C T1 complete conditioning (float32): NULL — a per-case convention flag changes nothing on the fastback cases (ISLA 0.120 vs 0.121, GeoTransolver 0.105 vs 0.111) and nothing in-family; with the full source kept, mixing 794 estate cars costs ISLA 17% and GeoTransolver 4% {#sec-nb-campc-t1-verdict}

**Setting.** T1 of campaign C (`studies/campaign_c_transfer/PREREG.md`)
asks whether the compound mismatch between DrivAerML's and SHIFT-SUV's
conventions (solver, ground and wheel treatment) is partly an
identifiability problem: two families trained together might blur into one
average if the model cannot tell which convention a case follows. The
instrument is a constant per-cell scalar, 0 for every DrivAerML case and 1
for every SHIFT-SUV case, handed to ISLA as a boundary scalar and to the
unit-drive GeoTransolver as a seventh functional channel; the unconditioned
twins train on the same mixed data (the full 435 DrivAerML train cars plus
the 794 estate cars, 1,229 cases) with the flag absent. Two seeds per arm,
500 epochs, lr 1e-3, frozen protocol; float32 inference under the
program-wide evaluation snapshot, no skipped loads in any log. The fastback
evaluation carries the flag value 1, since fastback shares estate's
conventions. Bars: conditioning MATTERS if the conditioned fastback error is
≥ 15% below its unconditioned twin for either architecture; NULL within 5%;
between, reported; an in-family (DrivAerML validation) cost above 5% is
reported as such.

**Readout (seed means, seeds in parentheses; artifact
`studies/campaign_c_transfer/campaign_c_t1_2026-09-10.json`).**

| arm | fastback pressure | fastback wall shear | fastback drag rel. MAE | DrivAerML pressure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA, no flag | 0.120 (0.116, 0.123) | 0.139 | 0.184 | 0.0652 |
| ISLA, convention flag | 0.121 (0.120, 0.122) | 0.141 | 0.152 | 0.0662 |
| GeoTransolver unit drive, no flag | 0.105 (0.105, 0.105) | 0.127 | 0.115 | 0.0525 |
| GeoTransolver unit drive, convention flag | 0.111 (0.109, 0.112) | 0.128 | 0.123 | 0.0529 |

: All four arms train on 435 DrivAerML + 794 estate cars. Drag: the recipe's integrated drag coefficient, mean absolute error over the reference mean (0.75). {#tbl-campc-t1}

**Verdict: NULL for ISLA (the flag moves the fastback error by 1.2% in the
wrong direction, 0.001 worse), "between" for GeoTransolver on the wrong
side (5.2% worse, 0.005), in-family cost 1.5% and 0.8%, both inside the 5%
clause.** The seed spreads (0.007 for ISLA, 0.003 for GeoTransolver) cover
the ISLA difference and most of GeoTransolver's; neither architecture
extracts anything from knowing which convention a case follows. The
reading is the second of the two preregistered ones: the mismatch is not
recoverable from a flag, and what the estate family buys the fastback cases
is coverage of its conventions in the data, not identification of them.
This fits the geometry of the problem: the conventions differ in the flow
the surface sees (ground clearance, rotating wheels, solver), which the
model reads off the boundary geometry and the pressure field it is fitting,
so a one-bit label adds no information the inputs did not already carry.

**Mixing cost with the source kept whole (the question ISLA Main asked).**
The T2 decomposition (@tbl-campc-t2-decomp) measured the mixing cost at a
50% foreign share with the source halved: 8% (ISLA) and 4% (GeoTransolver)
on the DrivAerML validation pressure. The unconditioned T1 arms are the
same measurement at a 65% foreign share with the source kept whole (435 +
794), so the halving factor is absent and the whole in-family rise is
mixing:

| architecture | 435 DrivAerML alone | 435 + 794 estate | mixing factor, full source | mixing factor, T2 (218 + 217) | fastback, 435 + 794 | fastback, 218 + 217 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA | 0.0557 | 0.0652 | 1.171 | 1.078 | 0.120 | 0.128 |
| GeoTransolver, unit drive | 0.0504 | 0.0525 | 1.042 | 1.043 | 0.105 | 0.115 |

: DrivAerML validation pressure relative L2 and fastback pressure relative L2, float32, two-seed means. Artifacts `campaign_c_t1_2026-09-10.json` (arms `cond0_*`, `ref_single_*`) and `campaign_c_t2_2026-09-10.json`. {#tbl-campc-t1-mixing}

So the 17% in-family rise of the 1,229-case ISLA model is entirely mixing,
and ISLA's mixing cost grows with the foreign share (8% at half, 17% at two
thirds) while GeoTransolver's does not (4% at either share). The extra 577
estate cars buy the fastback cases only 6% (ISLA) and 9% (GeoTransolver)
over the 217-car mix, so the estate coverage saturates early, as the T2
verdict suggested. The picture across T1–T3 is one statement with three
measurements: the unit-drive GeoTransolver holds its DrivAerML fit while
absorbing a second family (4% cost at either share) and carries 31% of its
DrivAerML pretraining into a 20-label adaptation; ISLA pays a mixing cost
that scales with the foreign share and carries nothing into adaptation.
Both agree that a convention flag is worthless and that coverage saturates
by a few hundred sibling cars.

**What changes.** Campaign C is complete. The transfer levers for this
program's setting rank: coverage (a few hundred cases of a sibling family,
T2) above few-shot adaptation (20 labels, GeoTransolver only, T3) above
conditioning (nothing, T1); the architectural gap they expose is ISLA's
family-specific DrivAerML fit, the target of the interior-context and
measure-consistent directions elsewhere in this book. Caveat: one flag
design (a constant one-bit scalar); a flag carrying the physical conditions
that differ (ground clearance, wheel rotation) is a different experiment,
but the T1 result says the model already reads those from the inputs.
Chapter @sec-campaigns-conditioning is written from this entry.
